title: Sum of Two Numbers
description: Write a function sum(a, b) that returns the addition of two numbers a and b.
hint: Use the addition operator (+) to add parameter a and parameter b.

title: Check Even or Odd
description: Write a function isEven(n) that returns true if the integer n is even, and false if it is odd.
hint: Check the remainder when dividing by 2 using the modulo operator (n % 2 === 0).

title: String Length Counter
description: Write a function getStringLength(str) that returns the total count of characters in str.
hint: Strings in JavaScript have a built-in .length property.

title: Check Positive Number
description: Write a function isPositive(n) that returns true if n is strictly greater than 0, otherwise false.
hint: Use the greater-than comparison operator: return n > 0;

title: Maximum of Two Numbers
description: Write a function maxOfTwo(a, b) that returns the larger number between a and b.
hint: You can use an if statement (a > b ? a : b) or Math.max(a, b).

title: Greeting Generator
description: Write a function createGreeting(name) that takes a name string and returns 'Hello, <name>!'.
hint: Use template literals `Hello, ${name}!` or string concatenation.

title: Sum of Array Elements
description: Write a function sumArray(arr) that computes and returns the sum of all numerical values in arr.
hint: Iterate with a for-loop or use arr.reduce((acc, n) => acc + n, 0).

title: Count Occurrences
description: Write a function countOccurrences(arr, target) that returns how many times target appears in arr.
hint: Initialize a count variable to 0, loop through arr, and increment count whenever item === target.

title: Reverse a String
description: Write a function reverseString(str) that returns a new string with the characters in reverse order.
hint: You can split into array, reverse, and join: str.split('').reverse().join('');

title: FizzBuzz Variant
description: Write a function fizzBuzz(n) returning 'FizzBuzz' if n is divisible by 3 and 5, 'Fizz' if divisible by 3, 'Buzz' if divisible by 5, or String(n).
hint: Check the combined condition (n % 15 === 0) first before checking 3 or 5 individually.

title: Filter Even Numbers
description: Write a function getEvensOnly(arr) that filters out odd numbers and returns a new array with only the even numbers.

title: Find Longest Word Length
description: Write a function findLongestWordLength(sentence) that returns the length of the longest word in the space-separated sentence string.
hint: Split sentence by space ' ' into words and find the max length with Math.max(...words.map(w => w.length)).

title: Debug Negative Max Bug
description: Fix the bug in findMax(arr) so that it correctly returns the maximum value in arr, even when all elements are negative or length is 1.
hint: Initialize max to arr[0] (or -Infinity) and fix the loop bounds to i < arr.length.

title: Recursive Factorial
description: Write a recursive function factorial(n) calculating the factorial of non-negative integer n. factorial(0) is 1.
hint: Base case: if n <= 1 return 1; Recursive step: return n * factorial(n - 1);

title: Fibonacci Number
description: Write a function fibonacci(n) that returns the n-th Fibonacci number where fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1, fib(2)=1, fib(3)=2...
hint: You can use an iterative approach with two variables a=0, b=1 or recursion with memoization.

title: Palindrome Checker
description: Write a function isPalindrome(str) returning true if str reads the same forward and backward (case-insensitive, ignoring non-alphanumeric characters).

input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

hint: Sanitize string: const cleaned = str.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, ''); and compare with cleaned.split('').reverse().join('');

title: Two Sum Target Indices
description: Write a function twoSum(nums, target) that returns the 0-based indices of the two numbers in nums that add up to target.
hint: Use a map of seen numbers to their indices: if target - nums[i] exists in map, return [map[target - nums[i]], i].

title: Flatten 2D Array
description: Write a function flattenArray(arr) that takes an array of arrays and flattens it into a single one-dimensional array.
hint: Use arr.flat() or arr.reduce((acc, sub) => acc.concat(sub), []);
